claims: Nowruz is the Persian New Year.
Nowruz is 3,000 years old.
Nowruz heralds the arrival of spring.
Nowruz heralds the vernal equinox.
The vernal equinox typically occurs March 20-21.
Over 300 million people celebrate Nowruz.
Nowruz symbolizes renewal.
Nowruz symbolizes rejuvenation.
Nowruz symbolizes the triumph of light over darkness.
Nowruz marks the first day of the Iranian calendar.
Nowruz is marked by family gatherings.
Nowruz is marked by street festivals.
Nowruz is marked by setting the Haft-Sin table.
The Haft-Sin table holds seven symbolic items representing nature.
Nowruz is a secular holiday.
Nowruz is rooted in Zoroastrianism.
Nowruz represents a fresh start.
Nowruz represents the rebirth of nature.
Families set a Haft-Sin table with seven items starting with the Persian letter 'S'.
The Haft-Sin table typically includes Sabzeh (wheat sprouts for renewal).
The Haft-Sin table typically includes Samanu (sweet pudding for strength).
The Haft-Sin table typically includes Senjed (dried fruit for love).
The Haft-Sin table typically includes Seer (garlic for health).
The Haft-Sin table typically includes Seeb (apple for beauty).
The Haft-Sin table typically includes Somāq (sumac for sunrise).
The Haft-Sin table typically includes Serkeh (vinegar for patience).
Ahead of Nowruz, people clean their homes (khooneh takouni).
People jump over fires during Chaharshanbe Suri to burn away negativity.
Nowruz celebrations last 13 days.
Nowruz celebrations conclude on Sizdebedar.
Sizdebedar is April 1 or 2.
Sizdebedar is a day spent picnicking outdoors to avoid bad luck.
Sabzi Polo ba Mahi is rice with herbs and fish.
Ash-e Reshteh is noodle soup.
Sabzi Polo ba Mahi is a traditional Nowruz food.
Ash-e Reshteh is a traditional Nowruz food.
Nowruz is observed in Iran.
Nowruz is observed in Azerbaijan.
Nowruz is observed in Afghanistan.
Nowruz is observed in Central Asia.
Nowruz is observed by diaspora communities worldwide.
The UN recognizes Nowruz as International Nowruz Day.
